the energy performance of a building is not only dependent on the building management system, but it is also influenced by occupant behaviour.

a building can be designed and built to state-of-the art principles, but it is the human dimension that makes the difference between high or low performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the human dimension of energy efficiency and the interaction between building management and occupants.
the human dimension of building energy performance.
the interrelationship of human and technology in the built environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the building is in good conditions, but it is not operated in the way it was designed for.

the energy management of a building is a complex task that requires a thorough understanding of building operation and occupant behaviour, and a continuous monitoring and evaluation of the building performance.
the energy management and control of the building was not in line with the design intentions, but the building management system was not to be blamed for this.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
building management and control technologies alone are not sufficient for achieving high performance.
the human factor is a key element in the operation of buildings and it has to be considered in the design and management of buildings.
a building management system is only effective when it is used by building operators and building users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the building management system should not be operated by untrained building operators.
building management systems can be used to achieve high energy performance in buildings but they require proper operation and maintenance and a well-informed building operator.
the human dimension of buildings should be considered in building design, operation and energy management.
